deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no mathematics. It is a library loan request slip, almost certainly for the Göttingen University Library, dated in red 'Juli 19. 55' (19 July 1855) and signed 'B Riemann, Dr phil.' with his address, apparently Weender Straße. The items requested are as follows.

(1) Crelle's Journal für die reine und angewandte Mathematik, volumes 44–47. The ink line gives the years 1852, 53, 54, 55; that line is crossed out in pencil, presumably by the librarian.

(2) Hermite's note on Abelian functions 'tiré des Comptes rendus', i.e. an offprint from the Comptes rendus. The whole entry is struck through in pencil, probably meaning 'not available' or 'not held'. This is most plausibly Hermite's 1855 note on the transformation of Abelian functions in genus 2, 'Sur la théorie de la transformation des fonctions abéliennes', Comptes rendus 40 (1855). The slip itself seems to read '[Théorie, struck] sur la composition des fonctions Abéliennes'. Either way, it bears directly on Riemann's own work then in progress on Abelian functions (published 1857).

(3) Strümpell, 'Kritik der Herbart…schen Metaphysik'. The adjective is partly struck, and the entry is struck through in pencil. This is almost certainly Ludwig Strümpell, 'Die Hauptpunkte der Herbart'schen Metaphysik kritisch beleuchtet' (1840). It fits Riemann's documented engagement with Herbart's philosophy in his philosophical fragments. A pencilled '1853' stands to the right, probably a librarian's annotation.

(4) 'Beer's Optik' – August Beer, Einleitung in die höhere Optik (Braunschweig, 1853). It is underlined. A pencilled '1854' stands below and to the right, perhaps a shelf or acquisition note.

A large pencilled '2' and connecting lines are library processing marks.

The next page is a duplicate slip for the same Crelle volumes, signed 'Privatdocent hier'. The previous page contains unrelated sketches of circles and of the line 0, 1, 2, ∞ (possibly cuts or domains for a function with branch points 0, 1, ∞).

There are no derivations to reconstruct.

results.what: Bibliographic evidence that in July 1855 Riemann requested Crelle vols. 44–47, a Hermite Comptes rendus note on Abelian functions, Strümpell's critique of Herbart's metaphysics, and Beer's Einleitung in die höhere Optik.
results.modern_name: Reading record / library loan slip (no mathematical content)

deep.surprise_reason: A library request slip with no mathematics. Riemann's interests in Abelian functions, Herbart's philosophy and optics or mathematical physics in 1853–55 are well documented. At most it gives minor biographical detail (the Hermite request in July 1855, and his address).
transcription_corrections: 'Kritik der Herbart Lotzen[?] Metaphysik' should most likely read 'Herbart'schen Metaphysik' (part of the adjective struck). The work is Strümpell's critique of Herbart's metaphysics; no reference to Lotze is evident.

The Hermite title 'Théorie sur la composition…' is better read as '[Théorie, struck] sur la composition des fonctions Abéliennes'. The entire Hermite entry and the Strümpell entry are struck through in pencil, not only the first word.
'1852. 53. 54. 55' is crossed out in pencil, as the bracket marking indicates. '1853' and '1854' are separate pencil annotations, probably by the library, not part of Riemann's ink text.
'Juli 19. 55.' is written in red ink, probably a library date stamp in manuscript.
The address is likely 'Weenderstraße' (Weender Straße, Göttingen); the house number is illegible.
